Context: Preconditions for setting alarms in the GUI, including initializing the system and ensuring the user is authenticated.

Sequence Diagram 1: Setting the HIGH RR Alarm Threshold
Participants: User, GUI, System

1. User -> GUI: "Start Alarm Settings"
2. GUI -> User: "Select HIGH RR Alarm Threshold"
3. User -> GUI: "Enter Threshold Value (5-30 in increments of 1)"
4. GUI -> User: "Threshold Accepted"
5. User -> System: "Save Settings"

Context: Preconditions for setting the LOW RR Alarm Threshold
Participants: User, GUI, System

6. User -> GUI: "Select LOW RR Alarm Threshold"
7. GUI -> User: "Enter Threshold Value (5-30 in increments of 1)"
8. User -> GUI: "Threshold Accepted"
9. User -> System: "Save Settings"

Sequence Diagram 2: Setting the Apnea Alarm Threshold
Participants: User, GUI, System

10. User -> GUI: "Select Apnea Alarm Threshold"
11. GUI -> User: "Enter Threshold Value (1-30 seconds in increments of 1)"
12. User -> GUI: "Threshold Accepted"
13. User -> System: "Save Settings"

Context: Preconditions for detecting an alarm when the relief valve opens
Participants: System, User

14. System -> User: "Monitor Relief Valve Status"
15. User -> System: "Detect Relief Valve Opening"
16. System -> System: "Check for Unexpected Flow Increase"
17. System -> User: "Alarm Triggered if Relief Valve Opens"

Context: Testing for invalid threshold values
Participants: User, GUI, System

18. User -> GUI: "Select HIGH RR Alarm Threshold"
19. GUI -> User: "Enter -1 (invalid value)"
20. GUI -> User: "Error: Invalid threshold value"
21. User -> System: "Save Settings" (expected rejection)

22. User -> GUI: "Select LOW RR Alarm Threshold"
23. GUI -> User: "Enter -1 (invalid value)"
24. GUI -> User: "Error: Invalid threshold value"
25. User -> System: "Save Settings" (expected rejection)

26. User -> GUI: "Select Apnea Alarm Threshold"
27. GUI -> User: "Enter -1 (invalid value)"
28. GUI -> User: "Error: Invalid threshold value"
29. User -> System: "Save Settings" (expected rejection)

Context: Testing for threshold beyond the upper bound
Participants: User, GUI, System

29. User -> GUI: "Select HIGH RR Alarm Threshold"
30. GUI -> User: "Enter 31 (above upper bound)"
31. GUI -> User: "Error: Threshold exceeds maximum allowed value"
32. User -> System: "Save Settings" (expected rejection)

Context: Testing for default threshold values
Participants: System, User

33. System -> User: "Display Default Thresholds"
34. User -> System: "Confirm Default Values are Displayed"

Context: Testing for step size verification
Participants: User, GUI, System

35. User -> GUI: "Select HIGH RR Alarm Threshold"
36. GUI -> User: "Enter 5 (valid value)"
37. User -> GUI: "Enter 6 (valid value, increment of 1)"
38. User -> GUI: "Enter 7 (valid value, increment of 1)"
39. User -> System: "Save Settings"

Context: Testing for apnea alarm lower bound
Participants: User, GUI, System

40. User -> GUI: "Select Apnea Alarm Threshold"
41. GUI -> User: "Enter 1 (lower bound)"
42. User -> System: "Save Settings"

Context: Testing for specific error messages
Participants: User, GUI

43. User -> GUI: "Select HIGH RR Alarm Threshold"
44. GUI -> User: "Enter 5 (valid value)"
45. GUI -> User: "Enter 4 (invalid value, not an increment of 1)"
46. GUI -> User: "Error: Threshold value must be in increments of 1"
47. User -> System: "Save Settings" (expected rejection)

48. User -> GUI: "Select Apnea Alarm Threshold"
49. GUI -> User: "Enter 1 (lower bound)"
50. GUI -> User: "Enter 0.5 (invalid value, not an increment of 1)"
51. GUI -> User: "Error: Threshold value must be in increments of 1"
52. User -> System: "Save Settings" (expected rejection)

Context: Testing for rejection of invalid threshold values
Participants: User, GUI, System

53. System -> User: "Display Error Message for Invalid Input"
54. User -> System: "Expect Error Message for -1 (invalid threshold value)"

Context: Testing for correct UI feedback on invalid input
Participants: User, GUI

55. User -> GUI: "Enter -1 (invalid threshold value)"
56. GUI -> User: "Error Message Displayed"

This test suite addresses all the requirements, including the previously uncovered and negative test cases. It ensures that the system handles invalid inputs correctly, enforces the step size for threshold values, and tests the default values and rejection of values beyond the upper bound. The JSON test cases correspond to the sequence diagrams and cover all the specified requirements with concrete, checkable outcomes. The groundedness is maintained by using values and conditions as specified in the requirements, and negative values are handled appropriately. The test cases also include boundary and negative path coverage.
